analysis.title: [GSX] Global Reflections (30 Oct 2026)
key_insights: The market sold off into Halloween and the AI pain trade continued. Hyperscaler earnings left investors focused on AI funding and returns. Appetite to add risk outside AI is also weak ahead of the midterms and a decision on Iran.
The desk sees demand for trades uncorrelated to AI and oil at a record, and thinks pockets of Healthcare offer the best opportunities.

The broadening trade (SPXXAI Index) worked in October. SPXXAI had its 3rd best day of outperformance ever vs SPX. The desk urges caution on pockets that benefited mainly from a short squeeze if the growth outlook weakens.

Midterms: in a Democratic sweep, the desk's favorite long is Affordable Care Act Beneficiaries (GSHLCACA). Democrats are pushing to revive the enhanced ACA premium tax credits that expired at end-2025, which would help hospitals, outpatient providers and health insurers facing rising bad debt and uncompensated care.

In a Democratic sweep the desk also sees tailwinds for AI Power (GSENEPOW), because more power supply would be presented as a fix for electricity inflation. Policymaker agreement on who bears datacenter costs could weaken datacenter project economics and weigh on ex-Power AI hardware (GSTMTAIH).

Corporate tax (GSPUTAXP) is a topic to watch. Trump's veto power means midterms are unlikely to change tax law, so 2027-28 earnings are largely insulated. A higher tax rate later would put earnings and valuations at risk beyond 2029.

The desk revamped its Healthcare AI Beneficiaries Basket (GSHLCAIP) to cover diagnostics, genomic and biological data, lab automation and precision medicine, beyond drug discovery. Many constituents have reported productivity and commercial proof points, and the basket has outperformed the broader Healthcare sector (S5HLTH) YTD. It shows low correlation to AI, rates and oil.
The Systematic Trading Strategy team's Growth Value Rotator is another uncorrelated trade: L/O GSRHBUBG is +27% YTD and L/S GSRHBUBT is +18%. The team is hosting a webinar next week.

Software vs Semis (GSPUSOSE) is +88% from June lows, helped by the reversal in momentum and a more nuanced Software AI-disruption narrative. Software forward P/E went from 17x to 23x in four months, and it is much less exposed to short momentum than on January 1. Earnings should show where structural pressure exists and where moats hold.

Crypto cyber-attack headlines point to underpriced AI disruption in Insurance (GSXUINSU, GSXEINSU). The sector rallied defensively in October but could face underwriting headwinds, especially if broader risk relief rotates Financials flows back to banks.
The desk expects global cybersecurity TAM to keep growing as AI use cases expand. Leading firms are concentrated in the US (GSTMTCYB), and clients are showing more interest in global expressions.

European Banks had their worst month since March 2023. The desk does not expect significant OAT-Bund tightening near term and sees the underperformance as overdone given limited spillover risk and +200bp ROTE expansion to 2028E.
The desk likes buying Greek Banks (GSXEGRBK) after a 10% de-rating. Supports: 3Q NII beats vs consensus, the Alpha Bank CMD on Nov 5, and MSCI's DM upgrade in May 2027.

Japanese Banks (GSXAJMEB) have disconnected from solid earnings. BoJ signaling for a December hike sets them up for a year-end relief rally. The risk is that an 'escalate to de-escalate' strategy on Iran fails, bringing more inflation and rates pain.

European Defense (GSSBDEFE) is +13% over three weeks, helped by non-AI exposure and high short crowding. GS expects European defense spend to grow at an 8% CAGR over FY25-30E, while valuations imply declining medium-term earnings. The desk expects 3Q results and strategy updates to ease concerns and sees potential for a c.30% re-rating back to September 2025 valuation levels.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects an 8% CAGR in European defense spend over FY25-30E, and 3Q results and strategy updates should show progress on production ramps, earnings growth and cash generation, which could drive a c.30% re-rating.
tension_points.bear_case: Valuations imply declining medium-term earnings, investors worry about procurement and execution, and the recent rally was exaggerated by high short crowding and non-AI rotation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 3Q results and strategy updates that fail to show progress on production ramps, earnings growth and cash generation.

tension_points.bull_case: Solid fundamentals, +200bp ROTE expansion to 2028E, Greek bank NII beats, and a BoJ December hike for Japanese banks.
tension_points.bear_case: An 'escalate to de-escalate' strategy on Iran does not materialize, driving inflation and rates pain, and French sovereign stress could spill over.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure of the 'escalate to de-escalate' strategy, bringing incremental inflation and rates pain over coming weeks.
